cy-commandaria.varieties: Xynisteri and local Mavro, from vineyards at least 5 years old (raised from 4 by the 2017 amendment); low goblet-trained vines, at least 200 per decare (275 for vineyards planted up to 1969).
cy-commandaria.min_alcohol: Grapes picked overripe once the Department of Agriculture announces the harvest, then sun-dried (about two weeks) before pressing; no continuous presses. The single document lists at least 212 g/l sugar for Xynisteri and 258 g/l for Mavro at harvest, 390 to 450 g/l after drying, and at least 10% actual alcohol from fermentation; the 2017 amendment (Decree KDP 314/2016) lowers these to 204 and 230 g/l, at least 374 g/l after drying and 9.5% for the base wine, and raises the volatile-acidity limit to 30 meq/l.
cy-commandaria.ageing: At least 2 years in oak barrels; the 2016 decree adds grades by length of ageing.
cy-commandaria.styles: Two categories: liqueur wine (fortified after fermentation, since 2017 also with neutral alcohol of agricultural origin; sweetening with products from the zone allowed with approval) and wine from sun-dried grapes (unfortified).
cy-commandaria.other: Made from grapes of 14 villages in the Limassol hills (400 to 900 m): Agios Georgios Silikou, Agios Konstantinos, Agios Mamas, Agios Pavlos, Apsiou, Gerasa, Doros, Zoopigi, Kalo Chorio, Kapilio, Laneia, Louvaras, Monagri, Silikou. Fermentation must take place in the zone; the wine may leave only after fermentation (for fortification and other treatments). Irrigation allowed only with approval. Protected in the EU since 2006; production rules date from a Cypriot law of 1990.
